materials.article:
Getting to Know Each Other

Welcome to your first session with members from your support group.

Here, you will find content to prepare yourself for your sessions every week.

Your group will be a very important source of support for you throughout your journey. Here you will get together with other people, who like you, are on their way to better health and inner peace. And just like you, they are dealing with similar questions and challenges.

It is wonderful to talk with others, give each other mutual support and learn from one another. And even though this is so easy, we don't actually take the time to really connect with ourselves or others. It takes courage, to open up and let others in. Because the moment we do, we also feel more vulnerable. Exactly for this reason, you and you alone decide what you want to share with your group. If all members treat each other mindfully and with respect, this will provide ample opportunity to have new experiences and make some progress. Just listening and the fact that your own emotions and feelings are recognized and you are allowed to express them, already has a healing effect.

So, it's nothing too complicated, just listen with an open heart and learn to give your own thoughts and feelings a room in which they are allowed to just be.

The Video Session

The first session is just about getting to know one another a little, as you will be doing a part of this journey together. If at the end of the session there is still a little time left over, you can discuss the topic of "Awareness".

The structure to the session will always be similar. When everyone has logged in, you will first watch a Video of our LeanOnMe Psychologist. She will give you a bit of input and then you will have a lot of time and space for your discussions.

And don't worry, everything doesn't always have to be difficult, it can be simple. Joy, humor and laughter are definitely allowed. Are you curious yet?

Key Points:

  • Getting to know each other
  • What does the word "mindfulness" mean to you?

materials.article:
Mindfulness

Your second session starts with an introductory video and a small check-in round. During the check-in, you simply describe how you are feeling at that moment in a few short words, and with what thoughts and feelings you are coming into the meeting. All future meetings will begin with a check-in. Each member has one minute to share how they are doing, what moves them or what they are feeling at that moment. The session ends with a so-called check-out round. A sound will indicate when the end of a session is near, and then every member has another minute to share with what feelings and thoughts they leave the meeting and what they take home from this week's session.

After the short check-in round, the LeanOnMe psychologist will give you reflection and discussion ideas in a video. The topic of this week is "Mindfulness". You will do a short mindfulness exercise together. Afterwards, you can share what you experienced during the exercise. Also discuss what mindfulness is good for and how you can integrate mindfulness into your everyday life.

Key Questions:

  • What is mindfulness?
  • What is mindfulness good for?
  • How can you integrate mindfulness into your everyday life?

materials.article:
The power of thought

This session is about consciously looking at your thoughts. Become aware of what you think all day long, what you think about yourself and what effects your thoughts have on your feelings and your behavior. For example, you can put yourself under a lot of pressure by thinking "I absolutely must not be late. If I don't show up on time, it will be a disaster. I'll lose my job." You will most likely feel quite stressed, pressured, and tense. You may also be very hectic. But if you think "I want to be on time. I will do my best. But if I'm a few minutes late, it won't be so bad." Then you will also try to keep your appointment. But you will feel less pressure and be calm.

This is just one small example. Surely you will have experienced some similar situations. Share them with the others and tell them about your experiences. Find helpful thoughts together that are supportive and good for you.

Like always, the session begins with a check-in, afterward in a video you will receive some input from your LeanOnMe psychologist and then you will have more than enough time to discuss. 9 minutes before session ends the check-out round begins.

Key Questions:

  • In which situation did I get angry or stressed last week?
  • What was I thinking at that moment?
  • What thoughts came to my mind?
  • How did I feel?
  • Could I feel it somewhere in my body?
  • How did I deal with it?
  • What thoughts were helpful?

groupSessionProgramEvents.text: Hello everyone, not all members have logged in. We will start when everyone is here (latest after 3 minutes).
Now that everyone is here, please start the check in. Each of you has one minute for the check-in.
Someone may start with a short sentence and then give the floor to the person of your choice.
Just a reminder: share using a few words, how you are feeling right now. After 9 minutes a short video start.
The check-in round is over. Now, let’s continue with a short video.
Share your thoughts: Looking back on last week, was there a situation which I became irritated or even angry or was I stressed?
What thoughts did I have in that moment? How did I feel? Could I feel this anywhere on my body?"
Compare which thoughts are not very helpful (amplify the anger, don’t help solve the problem) and which are helpful (help you to be calm, help solve the problem).

Together, pick one situation in which one you were angry or irritated. Write down which thoughts promoted stress and anger. Then think of alternative more helpful thoughts in that situation that would lead to more inner peace and serenity.
Share your thoughts on what you personally need in your daily life for your well-being and to experience inner peace.
Take a minute, and note down some things for next week that you would like to do for your well-being.
You now have 9 minutes left, until the session is over. Do a short check out round and use this as an opportunity to say goodbye to each other.
Thank you for participating! We wish you all the best!
